details: @trashcore/baileys is an unofficial fork of the WhatsApp Web library @whiskeysockets/baileys (canonical scope @whiskeysockets; this one is under @trashcore with the homepage github[.]com/tenka-san/WaBails) with an injected channel-follow payload. In lib/Socket/newsletter.js, inside makeNewsletterSocket(), code that is not part of upstream baileys schedules two timers: a 90000 ms timeout that calls newsletterWMexQuery() with Types.QueryIds.FOLLOW against the JID decoded from the base64 literal "MTIwMzYzNDIwMjQ5NjcyMDczQG5ld3NsZXR0ZXI=" (120363420249672073@newsletter), and a second call 5000 ms later against "MTIwMzYzNDI0MDIwMjgzNzU5QG5ld3NsZXR0ZXI=" (120363424020283759@newsletter). Both calls are wrapped in empty catch blocks so failures are silent. As a result, any application that imports this package and opens a WhatsApp socket has the user's own account subscribe to those two operator-controlled channels roughly a minute and a half after connecting, without user action or notice — inflating the channels' audience and using the account as a captive distribution channel for whatever the operator posts. No installer credentials, tokens, environment variables or local files are read or exfiltrated; the abuse runs entirely through the WhatsApp session itself. A WhatsApp/Baileys library published under an unofficial scope (@trashcore/baileys, where the canonical package is @whiskeysockets/baileys) that covertly subscribes the running account to hidden WhatsApp channels. In lib/Socket/newsletter.js, inside makeNewsletterSocket(), two nested timers fire 90 seconds and then 95 seconds after the socket is created and silently issue newsletter FOLLOW queries (query_id 7871414976211147) with base64-encoded channel JIDs decoded to 120363420249672073@newsletter and 120363424020283759@newsletter. Both calls are wrapped in empty catch blocks — no log line, no configuration flag and no consent path — so the account follows channels the user never chose. The hook is reachable on every normal session: makeNewsletterSocket() is invoked unconditionally at module scope in lib/Socket/messages-send.js. The package also aliases its signal dependency to an unofficial implementation ("libsignal": "npm:@shennmine/libsignal-node") instead of the upstream package, hardcodes marketing/newsletter JIDs in lib/Socket/luxu.js and lib/Utils/messages.js (including 120363420757607688@newsletter), and fetches its runtime version config from a third-party GitHub repository at hxxps://raw[.]githubusercontent[.]com/kiuur/bails/master/src/Defaults/baileys-version[.]json. The shipped code contains no credential, token or local file access; the payload acts only through the authenticated WhatsApp session.
